1.explanation: We import the Carbon CSS and the React TextInput component, then render it with both the `fluid` and `skeleton` props. According to the spec the skeleton variant should render two grey bars (one 8px high for the label, one 16px high for the input) spaced by 8px and with a 16px left margin. By running this code (e.g. in your CRA or Storybook setup) you will observe that nothing shows up – demonstrating that the skeleton state is missing in the fluid TextInput. This minimal sandbox reproduces exactly the bug shown in the screenshot.
1.bug_scenario: In the Fluid variant of the TextInput component we should get a skeleton placeholder—the grey “loading” bar in place of the label and the input—but nothing is rendered. In the screenshot you can see that the default (non-fluid) TextInput skeleton renders two grey bars (one 8px high for the label, one 16px high for the input), spaced 8px apart, with a 16px gutter on the left. When you try to turn on skeleton mode for the fluid TextInput (using the skeleton and fluid props together), you get no grey bars at all.
